title: Abstract Geometric vs Neo-Swiss
lede: Both are compositions made of circles, squares and type on a grid. One uses shape as the layout; the other uses columns and never draws a shape at all.
verdict: Abstract geometric places a large circle and a rotated square as the structure itself, then fits the type against them. Neo-Swiss has no shapes: a 12-column grid, a headline across nine columns, a standfirst starting at column seven, and one red used twice.
brief: The abstract page has geometry you can see. A circle at 50% radius, a square rotated 18 degrees with a 28px radius, pill buttons at 999px, cards at 24px with a 1px #ece6dd hairline. The headline is capped at 16ch because it has to sit in the gap the shapes leave, not because it needs a measure.

Neo-Swiss has geometry you can only infer. Everything is placed on repeat(12, 1fr): the headline takes 1 / span 9, the standfirst 7 / span 5, so the two blocks overlap across three columns. Corners are 0 everywhere, there are no shadows, and red appears exactly twice on the page.

dimensions.name: Layout device
dimensions.a: Shapes define space; text fits around them

dimensions.name: Accent
dimensions.a: Pastel fills at low opacity, blending where they overlap

cssDelta.label: Structure
cssDelta.a: shapes as blocks, text fitted against them

whenA: The page has few words and needs a composition to hold the eye
You want a modern, designed feel without photography
The brand is creative and can carry a pastel palette
whenB: The page carries several kinds of content and needs a system rather than a composition
The brand is institutional — finance, engineering, academia — where restraint reads as competence
You want the layout itself to look designed while staying entirely in black and white plus one red
promptDelta: The instruction that separates them is whether shapes are allowed. For abstract geometric, name the shapes and their sizes — one circle at 50%, one 28px square rotated 18 degrees — and say the text is fitted against them. For neo-Swiss, state the column spans for the headline and the standfirst explicitly and forbid decorative shapes entirely. A model asked for "geometric layout" will add circles to a Swiss grid, which produces neither: columns that justify nothing, decorated with shapes that align to nothing.
